entries.sampleCode:
Complete invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or exchange conversion):

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}
```

Complete Frozen 4.0 navigation report:

```xpath
(: Partner invoice batch: navigate JNodes, unwrap each invoice map for reporting. :)
let $tree := jtree(parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}'))
return string-join($tree / invoices / * ! (let $invoice := jvalue(.) return concat($invoice?id, '/', $invoice?currency, ':', format-number($invoice?total, '0.00'))), ';')
```

Complete portable 3.1 alternative:

```xpath
(: Portable 3.1: plain map/array lookup, without JNode identity or parent context. :)
let $batch := parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}')
return string-join($batch?invoices?* ! concat(?id, '/', ?currency, ':', format-number(?total, '0.00')), ';')
```

Both return exactly:

```text
INV-1042/EUR:30.00;INV-1043/USD:12.00
```

Empty input:

```json
{"invoices":[]}
```

Both complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-empty.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-empty.xpath) expressions return the empty string. Reordered input:

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12},{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30}]}
```

The complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-reordered.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-reordered.xpath) expressions return:

```text
INV-1043/USD:12.00;INV-1042/EUR:30.00
```

Confirmed broader identity boundary:

```xpath
let $tree := jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) return $tree is $tree
```

Result: `XPTY0004`. Complete node-type probes:

```xpath
jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) instance of node()
```

Result: `false`.

```xpath
parse-xml('<invoice/>') instance of xnode()
```

Result: `XPST0051`.

entries.sampleCode:
Complete [batch input](../examples/capturing-accumulators/input.xml):

```xml
<batch><invoice id="INV-2048" currency="EUR"><line sku="P100"/><line sku="P200"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-2049" currency="USD"><line sku="P300"/></invoice></batch>
```

Complete [capture identity probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/main-observed.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred capturing accumulators and in-memory invoice alternatives.
SPECIAL NOTES: Capture attribute acceptance is not snapshot support; no streaming claim.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="4.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:accumulator name="latest" initial-value="()">
    <xsl:accumulator-rule match="invoice" phase="end" capture="yes" select="."/>
  </xsl:accumulator>
  <xsl:mode use-accumulators="latest"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:variable name="last" select="accumulator-after('latest')"/>
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':source=', $last is ., ':lines=', count($last/line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Observed principal text output:

```text
INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;
```

This is original-node retention, not the draft-required copy. The [version 3.0 probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture31.xsl) has the same observed result; the [ordinary 3.0 form](../examples/capturing-accumulators/ordinary31.xsl) removes the capture attribute and honestly expresses source retention.

### Explicit snapshot alternative

Complete [XSLT 3.0 snapshot stylesheet](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot31.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred capturing accumulators and in-memory invoice alternatives.
SPECIAL NOTES: Capture attribute acceptance is not snapshot support; no streaming claim.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:variable name="copy" select="snapshot(.)"/>
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':source=', $copy is ., ':lines=', count($copy/line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;
```

Line children survive the copy and identity differs. This snapshot is made in an ordinary template using an in-memory source; it does not enable the deferred rule or certify streaming memory behavior.

### Scalar projection alternative

Complete [XSLT 3.0 projection](../examples/capturing-accumulators/projection31.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred capturing accumulators and in-memory invoice alternatives.
SPECIAL NOTES: Capture attribute acceptance is not snapshot support; no streaming claim.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala

SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':lines=', count(line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2048:lines=2;INV-2049:lines=1;
```

### Empty and reordered input

Complete empty input:

```xml
<batch/>
```

The capture, snapshot and projection empty fixtures return the empty string. Complete reordered input:

```xml
<batch><invoice id="INV-2049" currency="USD"><line sku="P300"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-2048" currency="EUR"><line sku="P200"/><line sku="P100"/></invoice></batch>
```

Snapshot output:

```text
INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;
```

Bosak source reviewed 2026-10-12 at [revision 28d8dccc](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/28d8dccc74ab35e27db92584a7bc3e1a202b7cb5) (URI documentation delivery; engine version 1.1.2). This is a new disposition record, not a constructor implementation or tier promotion.

External reference: [XPath 4.0 node constructors](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-constructors). Immutable review source: [QT4CG expressions.xml at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), IDs `id-constructors` and `id-computedConstructors`.
The source records addition to XPath on 2026-02-07 (issue 2427 / PR 2446), and name-coercion changes on 2026-05-23. This current review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. The draft includes the feature; Bosak retains its deferral.
entries.sampleCode:
Complete [invoice input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/input.xml):

```xml
<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>
```

Complete [refused XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/main-refusal.xpath):

```xpath
let $i := parse-xml('<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>')/invoice
return element { 'receipt' } { attribute { 'id' } { string($i/@id) }, element { 'customer' } { string($i/customer) }, element { 'total' } { attribute { 'currency' } { string($i/amount/@currency) }, string($i/amount) } }
```

Observed outcome: `XPST0003`; no constructed receipt is returned.

### XPath 3.1 report alternative

Complete [text-report fixture](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $i := parse-xml('<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>')/invoice return concat('id=', $i/@id, '; customer=', $i/customer, '; total=', $i/amount, ' ', $i/amount/@currency)
```

Output:

```text
id=INV-2048; customer=Ada & Co; total=125.50 EUR
```

### Complete XSLT 3.0 construction alternative

The [stylesheet](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/xslt-main.xsl) consumes the input above, using `/invoice` as its template context. It documents its projection contract and empty-content boundary inside the file.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Project a supplier invoice into an ERP receipt using portable XSLT 3.0.
SPECIAL NOTES: Alternative to deferred computed XPath node constructors; no external I/O.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation

Input contract: invoice/@id, customer text, amount text and amount/@currency.
The stylesheet projects supplied strings; it does not validate currency or totals.
XSLT node construction escapes XML characters through the serializer.
Empty customer content creates an empty customer element. Attribute instructions
precede child nodes. No computed XPath constructor expression is required.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">
  <xsl:output method="xml" omit-xml-declaration="yes" indent="no"/>
  <xsl:template match="/invoice">
    <xsl:element name="receipt">
      <xsl:attribute name="id" select="string(@id)"/>
      <customer><xsl:value-of select="customer"/></customer>
      <total><xsl:attribute name="currency" select="string(amount/@currency)"/><xsl:value-of select="amount"/></total>
    </xsl:element>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Principal output (no secondary output):

```xml
<receipt id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><total currency="EUR">125.50</total></receipt>
```

Complete [empty-customer input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/empty.xml):

```xml
<invoice id="INV-EMPTY"><customer/><amount currency="EUR">0.00</amount></invoice>
```

Output:

```xml
<receipt id="INV-EMPTY"><customer/><total currency="EUR">0.00</total></receipt>
```

### Existing XQuery evidence

The existing `XQuery_ComputedElement_ComputedNameAndAtomicContent` test evaluates:

```xquery
(name(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 }), string(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 }))
```

It asserts two string items, `dyn` and `1 2 3`, through `XQueryCompiler` and `XQueryContext`. This is named unit-test evidence, not a new XQuery manifest fixture or proof that XPath constructors work.

entries.sampleCode:
Complete synthetic [batch input](../examples/enclosing-modes/input.xml):

```xml
<batch><invoice id="INV-2048" currency="EUR"><line sku="P100"/><line sku="P200"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-2049" currency="USD"><line sku="P300"/></invoice></batch>
```

Complete [refused 4.0 stylesheet](../examples/enclosing-modes/main-refusal4.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred enclosing modes and portable invoice export/audit dispatch.
SPECIAL NOTES: Named top-level rules are the supported alternative; no external I/O.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice attributes and ordered line/@sku values. Output: text report.
Invoice and line rules share the export mode. Explicit mode or #current retains
export dispatch during recursion; omitted mode uses the lexical default instead.
These projections do not validate invoice data or enforce enclosing-mode isolation.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns:erp="urn:example:erp" xmlns:q="urn:example:erp" version="4.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:mode name="erp:export">
    <xsl:template match="invoice">
      <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':', @currency, ':')"/>
      <xsl:apply-templates select="line"/>
      <xsl:text>;</xsl:text>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="line">
      <xsl:value-of select="concat(@sku, '/')"/>
    </xsl:template>
  </xsl:mode>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice" mode="erp:export"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Observed outcome: `XTSE0260`. No export result is asserted for this failing case.

### Complete portable XSLT 3.0 alternative

[Top-level named rules](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable3.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred enclosing modes and portable invoice export/audit dispatch.
SPECIAL NOTES: Named top-level rules are the supported alternative; no external I/O.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice attributes and ordered line/@sku values. Output: text report.
Invoice and line rules share the export mode. Explicit mode or #current retains
export dispatch during recursion; omitted mode uses the lexical default instead.
These projections do not validate invoice data or enforce enclosing-mode isolation.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns:erp="urn:example:erp" xmlns:q="urn:example:erp" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:mode name="erp:export"/>
  <xsl:template match="invoice" mode="erp:export">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':', @currency, ':')"/>
    <xsl:apply-templates select="line" mode="erp:export"/>
    <xsl:text>;</xsl:text>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="line" mode="erp:export">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@sku, '/')"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice" mode="erp:export"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Principal text output:

```text
INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;
```

The [version 4.0 comparison](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable4.xsl) returns the same report. The [current-mode fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/current-mode.xsl) uses `#current` for line recursion and returns the same report despite a competing unnamed line rule.

### Omitted recursion mode boundary

Complete [omitted-mode fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/omitted-recursion-mode.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred enclosing modes and portable invoice export/audit dispatch.
SPECIAL NOTES: Named top-level rules are the supported alternative; no external I/O.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice attributes and ordered line/@sku values. Output: text report.
Invoice and line rules share the export mode. Explicit mode or #current retains
export dispatch during recursion; omitted mode uses the lexical default instead.
These projections do not validate invoice data or enforce enclosing-mode isolation.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns:erp="urn:example:erp" xmlns:q="urn:example:erp" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:mode name="erp:export"/>
  <xsl:template match="invoice" mode="erp:export">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':', @currency, ':')"/>
    <xsl:apply-templates select="line"/>
    <xsl:text>;</xsl:text>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="line" mode="erp:export">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@sku, '/')"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="line">
    <xsl:text>wrong/</xsl:text>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice" mode="erp:export"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2048:EUR:wrong/wrong/;INV-2049:USD:wrong/;
```

The [lexical default fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/lexical-default-mode.xsl) sets the root `default-mode` to export and obtains the export report with omitted recursion. That is an explicit lexical policy, not enclosing-mode support.

### Empty and reordered input

Complete empty input:

```xml
<batch/>
```

Output is the empty string (zero principal text bytes). Complete reordered input:

```xml
<batch><invoice id="INV-2049" currency="USD"><line sku="P300"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-2048" currency="EUR"><line sku="P200"/><line sku="P100"/></invoice></batch>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2049:USD:P300/;INV-2048:EUR:P200/P100/;
```

The reverse-selection fixture reverses invoices without reversing their line sequence. The audit fixture reports `audit:INV-2048:2;audit:INV-2049:1;`, using its own top-level mode rules.

The partner's fragment can contain HTML that is not XML: ```html

Invoice
INV-1042

``` The complete [XML refusal expression](../examples/external-input-functions/xml-is-not-html.xpath) raises `FODC0006`; parse-xml is not an HTML5 parser. The integration host instead supplies a well-formed normalized invoice batch: ```xml ``` Complete portable XPath 3.1 report: ```xpath (: Host supplies well-formed invoice XML after acquisition/HTML normalization. :) let $batch := parse-xml('') return string-join($batch/invoices/invoice ! concat(@id, '/', @currency, ':', format-number(xs:decimal(@total), '0.00')), ';') ``` Exact output: ```text INV-1042/EUR:30.00;INV-1043/USD:12.00 ``` Empty input: ```xml ``` The [complete empty expression](../examples/external-input-functions/normalized-xml-empty.xpath) returns the empty string. Reordered input: ```xml ``` The [complete reordered expression](../examples/external-input-functions/normalized-xml-reordered.xpath) returns: ```text INV-1043/USD:12.00;INV-1042/EUR:30.00 ``` Fixed partner text record: ```text INV-1042|EUR|30.00 ``` Complete narrow alternative to a grammar-parser factory: ```xpath (: Fixed three-field partner record; no quotes, escapes, embedded pipes or grammar parser. :) let $record := 'INV-1042|EUR|30.00' return if ($record eq '') then '' else let $fields := tokenize($record, '\|') return concat($fields[1], '/', $fields[2], ':', format-number(xs:decimal($fields[3]), '0.00')) ``` Exact output: ```text INV-1042/EUR:30.00 ``` Already-acquired attachment bytes (the eight-byte `%PDF-1.7` prefix only, not a complete PDF or PDF validation): ```xpath (: Bytes already acquired by the host; this cast does not fetch a resource. :) string(xs:base64Binary(xs:hexBinary('255044462D312E37'))) ``` Exact base64 output: ```text JVBERi0xLjc= ``` Explicit business guard for an already parsed invoice: ```xml ``` Complete guard expression: ```xpath (: Business guard only; does not validate XSD or annotate nodes. :) let $invoice := parse-xml('')/invoice return if (string-length(string($invoice/@id)) gt 0 and $invoice/@currency = ('EUR','USD') and $invoice/@total castable as xs:decimal) then if (xs:decimal($invoice/@total) ge 0) then concat($invoice/@id, '/', $invoice/@currency, ':', format-number(xs:decimal($invoice/@total), '0.00')) else error(QName('urn:invoice', 'INVALID-INVOICE')) else error(QName('urn:invoice', 'INVALID-INVOICE')) ``` Exact output: ```text INV-1042/EUR:30.00 ``` A zero total remains valid: ```xml ``` Exact [zero guard](../examples/external-input-functions/invoice-guard-zero.xpath) output: ```text INV-1043/USD:0.00 ``` Invalid and missing business fields: ```xml ``` ```xml ``` Their complete [invalid](../examples/external-input-functions/invoice-guard-invalid.xpath) and [missing-field](../examples/external-input-functions/invoice-guard-empty.xpath) expressions report `INVALID-INVOICE`. entries.sampleCode:
The source represents two invoices in different currencies. INV-1042 totals `2 × 12.50 + 1 × 5 = 30.00 EUR`; INV-1043 totals `3 × 4 = 12.00 USD`.

```xml
<invoices><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR"><line sku="FILTER" quantity="2" price="12.50"/><line sku="BLUE" quantity="1" price="5"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD"><line sku="SEAL" quantity="3" price="4"/></invoice></invoices>
```

  <xsl:output method="text"/>

  <!-- The wrapper is a user function, not registration of the draft fn function. -->
  <xsl:function name="f:export" as="xs:string*">
    <xsl:param name="nodes" as="element(invoice)*"/>
    <xsl:param name="label" as="xs:string"/>

entries.sampleCode:
Complete invoice input; totals are precomputed and each amount retains its currency:

```xml
<invoices><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD" total="12"/><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR" total="30"/><invoice id="INV-1044" currency="EUR" total="0"/></invoices>
```

Complete XQuery 3.1 query:

```xquery
(: XQuery 3.1: select positive invoices and sort by currency then identifier. :)
xquery version "3.1";
let $batch := parse-xml('<invoices><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD" total="12"/><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR" total="30"/><invoice id="INV-1044" currency="EUR" total="0"/></invoices>')
return string-join((for $invoice in $batch/invoices/invoice
where xs:decimal($invoice/@total) gt 0
order by string($invoice/@currency), string($invoice/@id)
return concat($invoice/@id, '/', $invoice/@currency, ':', format-number(xs:decimal($invoice/@total), '0.00'))), ';')
```

Complete portable XPath 3.1 alternative:

```xpath
(: XPath 3.1: predicate filtering plus explicit sort key. :)
let $batch := parse-xml('<invoices><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD" total="12"/><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR" total="30"/><invoice id="INV-1044" currency="EUR" total="0"/></invoices>')
return string-join(sort($batch/invoices/invoice[xs:decimal(@total) gt 0], (), function($invoice){concat($invoice/@currency, '/', $invoice/@id)}) ! concat(@id, '/', @currency, ':', format-number(xs:decimal(@total), '0.00')), ';')
```

Both sorted positive-invoice reports return exactly:

```text
INV-1042/EUR:30.00;INV-1043/USD:12.00
```

The version boundary is a separate complete query:

```xquery
xquery version "4.0"; 1
```

Result: `XQST0031`. Observed XPath where extension:

```xpath
string-join((for $i in (3,1,2) where $i gt 1 return $i) ! string(.), '|')
```

Result: `3|2`, also checked at 4.0 and experimental. Complete forward-report stylesheet:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>

AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify invoice processing through ordinary and streaming XSLT paths.
SPECIAL NOTES: Exact report parity does not certify Streaming 4.0 or memory bounds.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: invoice XML. Output: one currency-labelled row per invoice, or the declared error.
Empty batches return empty text; reordered batches retain input order.

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <!-- A forward pass reports every invoice; sorting is a separate buffered task. -->
    <xsl:for-each select="invoices/invoice">
      <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, '/', @currency, ':', format-number(xs:decimal(@total), '0.00'), ';')"/>
    </xsl:for-each>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

entries.sampleCode:
Complete partner invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or currency conversion occurs here):

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"}]}
```

Portable XPath 3.1 JSON Lines export:

```xpath
(: Complete invoice batch; serialize each record separately and join with LF. :)
let $batch := parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"}]}')
return string-join($batch?invoices?* ! serialize(., map{'method':'json'}), codepoints-to-string(10))
```

Exact output, including one LF between the records and no terminal LF:

```text
{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1043"}
```

Empty input:

```json
{"invoices":[]}
```

The complete [empty expression](../examples/serialization-parameters/portable-json-lines-empty.xpath) returns the empty string. Reordered input:

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"},{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"}]}
```

The [complete reordered expression](../examples/serialization-parameters/portable-json-lines-reordered.xpath) returns:

```text
{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1043"}
{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
```

Observed fn:serialize solidus control boundary:

```xpath
serialize(map{'uri':'https://partner.example/invoices/1042'}, map{'method':'json','escape-solidus':false()})
```

Exact result (false is ignored):

```text
{"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
```

Shared XML input for all XSLT probes:

```xml
<invoices><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR" total="30" uri="https://partner.example/invoices/1042"/><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD" total="12" uri="https://partner.example/invoices/1043"/></invoices>
```

Supported XSLT 3.0 solidus alternative:

```xml

SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation

    <xsl:sequence select="string(invoices/invoice[1]/@uri)"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Practical case: [stock ledger](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath). The
[empty-movement case](../examples/fn-scan/edge.xpath) returns only the opening
balance, displayed as `100`. Both cases require `XPath40Experimental`; the
[earlier baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) runs at `XPath31`.

~~~xquery
fn:scan((1, 2, 3), 0, fn($acc, $it) { $acc + $it })
  (: → [0], [1], [3], [6] — every running total, init first :)

fn:scan((), "start", fn($acc, $it) { $acc || $it })
  (: → ["start"] — empty input yields just the init :)
~~~

entries.sampleCode:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>
```

### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>')/batch/reading
return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $first := min($codes)
return let $last := max($codes)
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

Exact output:

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

A, B and C supply valid decimals; D and E remain rejected identifiers. The ERP
namespace sorts before the QA namespace; within QA, `missing` is the last local
name. This explains the code endpoints without assigning a business rank.

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>')/batch/reading
return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return let $less := function($a, $b) {
  let $ns := compare(namespace-uri-from-QName($a), namespace-uri-from-QName($b), $cp)
  return if ($ns eq 0) then compare(local-name-from-QName($a), local-name-from-QName($b), $cp) lt 0 else $ns lt 0
}
return let $first := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($next, $best)) then $next else $best })
return let $last := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($best, $next)) then $next else $best })
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

Exact output:

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

The fold comparator performs two comparisons, preserving the namespace/local-name
ordering even when one namespace URI is a prefix of another. The numeric part
uses the same explicit decimal normalization policy as the 4.0 report.

entries.sampleCode:
Complete synthetic input: a gateway status-check sequence for invoice INV-2048.
The third response remains unread because the second response is accepted.

```xml
<submission id="INV-2048">
  <response status="pending"/>
  <response status="accepted"/>
  <response status="pending"/>
</submission>
```

### Test before the action

[Runnable while-do expression](../examples/bounded-retries/while-main.xpath):

```xpath
let $responses := parse-xml('<submission id="INV-2048"><response status="pending"/><response status="accepted"/><response status="pending"/></submission>')/submission/response
let $limit := 3
let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()}
let $advance := function($state, $position) {
  let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1])
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
let $final := while-do($initial, function($state, $position) { $state?status ne 'accepted' and $state?attempts lt $limit }, $advance)
return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted
```

### Test after the action

[Runnable do-until expression](../examples/bounded-retries/until-main.xpath):

```xpath
let $responses := parse-xml('<submission id="INV-2048"><response status="pending"/><response status="accepted"/><response status="pending"/></submission>')/submission/response
let $limit := 3
let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()}
let $advance := function($state, $position) {
  let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1])
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
let $final := if ($limit le 0) then $initial else do-until($initial, $advance, function($state, $position) { $state?status eq 'accepted' or $state?attempts ge $limit })
return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted
```

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable bounded fold](../examples/bounded-retries/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $responses := parse-xml('<submission id="INV-2048"><response status="pending"/><response status="accepted"/><response status="pending"/></submission>')/submission/response
return let $limit := 3
return let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()}
return let $advance := function($state, $position) {
  let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1])
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
return let $final := fold-left(1 to $limit, $initial, function($state, $position) { if ($state?status eq 'accepted') then $state else $advance($state, $position) })
return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted
```

### Exhausted budget

Replace the accepted response with pending. Complete input:

```xml
<submission id="INV-2048">
  <response status="pending"/>
  <response status="pending"/>
  <response status="pending"/>
</submission>
```

Both [while-do](../examples/bounded-retries/while-exhausted.xpath) and
[do-until](../examples/bounded-retries/until-exhausted.xpath) report:

```text
status=pending; attempts=3; exhausted=true; trace=pending,pending,pending
```

| [until-one-attempt](../examples/bounded-retries/until-one-attempt.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=1; exhausted=true; trace=pending` |
| [until-zero-budget](../examples/bounded-retries/until-zero-budget.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=0; exhausted=true; trace=` |
| [until-missing-status](../examples/bounded-retries/until-missing-status.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` |
| [while-initially-accepted](../examples/bounded-retries/while-initially-accepted.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=0; exhausted=false; trace=` |
| [until-initially-accepted](../examples/bounded-retries/until-initially-accepted.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` |
| [while-empty-decision](../examples/bounded-retries/while-empty-decision.xpath) | `0` |
| [until-empty-decision](../examples/bounded-retries/until-empty-decision.xpath) | `2` |
| [until-empty-state](../examples/bounded-retries/until-empty-state.xpath) | `1,2` |
| [while-sequence-state](../examples/bounded-retries/while-sequence-state.xpath) | `1,2,3,4` |
| [while-nonboolean](../examples/bounded-retries/while-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [while-noncallable-action](../examples/bounded-retries/while-noncallable-action.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [while-noncallable-predicate](../examples/bounded-retries/while-noncallable-predicate.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [while-action-error](../examples/bounded-retries/while-action-error.xpath) | `ATTEMPT` |
| [until-nonboolean](../examples/bounded-retries/until-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [until-noncallable-action](../examples/bounded-retries/until-noncallable-action.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [until-noncallable-predicate](../examples/bounded-retries/until-noncallable-predicate.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [until-action-error](../examples/bounded-retries/until-action-error.xpath) | `ATTEMPT` |

A zero budget reports exhausted without performing a check. A budget of one
stops after pending. An initially accepted state stays unchanged with `while-do`,
but the `do-until` variant consumes pending then accepted responses. A missing
first status uses pending and still reaches acceptance on attempt two.
The sequence-state fixtures prove that callbacks receive the whole sequence;
the empty-state fixture proves that empty input does not skip a do-until action.
An empty decision stops while-do immediately but continues do-until until its
second, true decision. Nonboolean/noncallable fixtures raise XPTY0004; an action
exception propagates without being retried automatically.

entries.sampleCode:
Complete synthetic input; the name contains e followed by combining acute, two interior spaces and a truck emoji:

```xml
<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>
```

### Complete XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $name := string(parse-xml('<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>')/customer/name)
let $label := trim-space($name)
return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(characters($label)), '; graphemes=', count(graphemes($label)), '; export=[', pad-string($label, 10, map {'padding': '.'}), ']; separator=', char(8212))
```

Exact output:

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; graphemes=7; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```

### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $name := string(parse-xml('<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>')/customer/name)
return let $label := replace(replace($name, '^\s+', ''), '\s+$', '')
return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(string-to-codepoints($label)), '; export=[', $label, string-join(for $i in 1 to max((0, 10 - string-length($label))) return '.', ''), ']; separator=', codepoints-to-string(8212))
```

Exact output:

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```

Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats.

**Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/main.xpath)

```xquery
(: One array member holds all product codes for one order. :)
let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}),
    $members := array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}),
    $batch := array:slice($members, 1, 2)
return concat('orders=', array:size($batch), ';lines=', string-join(array:items($batch), ','))
```

Expected text:

```text
orders=2;lines=FILTER-A,SEAL-B,VALVE-C
```

**Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/baseline.xpath)

let $path := string(parse-xml('<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>')/file/@path)

Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>
```

### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/measurement-comparison/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>')/readings/reading
return string-join(for $row in $rows return
  let $value := if (string($row/@value) = '') then () else
    if ($row/@kind = 'decimal') then xs:decimal($row/@value) else
    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $order := compare($value, $limit)
    return if ($order lt 0) then 'below' else if ($order eq 0) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

Exact output:

```text
A=at-limit;B=above;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

A is decimal 2 against decimal 2. B and C share the decimal limit 3.1 but retain
their distinct binary representations. D contains numeric NaN and E has no value;
both are reported as missing instead of being silently ranked below the limit.

    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $normalized := xs:double($value)
    return let $boundary := xs:double($limit)
    return if ($normalized lt $boundary) then 'below' else if ($normalized eq $boundary) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

Exact output:

```text
A=at-limit;B=at-limit;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

This is a different numeric policy, not an exact 3.1 implementation of the 4.0
atomic-ordering function. Stringifying the numbers and calling 3.1 `compare`
would instead compare their text and would be unsuitable for numeric limits.

Complete synthetic schedule input:

```xml
<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
let $days := days-in-month(build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': 1}))
let $cutoff := build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': $days, 'hours': xs:integer($schedule/@hours), 'minutes': xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), 'seconds': 0, 'timezone': xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)})
return concat('days=', $days, '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
return let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
return let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
return let $first := xs:date(concat(format-integer($year, '0000'), '-', format-integer($month, '00'), '-01'))
return let $last := $first + xs:yearMonthDuration('P1M') - xs:dayTimeDuration('P1D')
return let $local := dateTime($last, xs:time(concat(format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@hours), '00'), ':', format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), '00'), ':00')))
return let $cutoff := adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($local, xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone))
return concat('days=', day-from-date($last), '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```

entries.sampleCode:
The synthetic fixture represents a warehouse queue in arrival order. ORD103 is
held for investigation; ORD104 must wait behind it despite its ready status.

```xml
<queue>
  <order id="ORD101" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD102" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD103" status="hold"/>
  <order id="ORD104" status="ready"/>
</queue>
```

Complete XPath 4.0 expression ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
let $ready := function($order, $position) { string($order/@status) eq 'ready' }
let $dispatch := take-while($queue, $ready)
let $retained := drop-while($queue, $ready)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104
```

Complete XPath 3.1 comparison ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
return let $stop := ((for $i in 1 to count($queue) return if (string($queue[$i]/@status) eq 'ready') then () else $i)[1], count($queue) + 1)[1]
return let $dispatch := subsequence($queue, 1, $stop - 1)
return let $retained := subsequence($queue, $stop)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Its exact output is identical. A whole-queue filter instead returns
`ORD101,ORD102,ORD104`, as the [filter comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath)
verifies. It would allow ORD104 to overtake the held order.

### Boundary and callback cases

Each file embeds its complete input. Empty output below means an empty string
from the report's `string-join`, not a string returned by the selection function.

| Runnable case | Exact result or error | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| [main](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Normal ordered split |
| [baseline](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Earlier-version equivalent |
| [filter-comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104` | Independent ready-order policy |
| [all-ready](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/all-ready.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104; retained=` | No blocker |
| [first-held](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/first-held.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | First order blocks all work |
| [empty](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/empty.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=` | No orders |
| [missing-status](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/missing-status.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Missing status blocks dispatch |
| [position-cap](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/position-cap.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | One-based capacity boundary |
| [reconstruction](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/reconstruction.xpath) | `true` | Both parts restore input |
| [map-predicate](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/map-predicate.xpath) | `ready,ready` | Status map used as callable |
| [take-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-empty-decision.xpath) | `(empty string)` | Empty decision stops immediately |
| [take-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [take-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [take-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD101` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |
| [drop-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-empty-decision.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102` | Empty decision retains everything |
| [drop-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [drop-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [drop-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD102,ORD103` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |

For the missing-status case the full input is the XML above with ORD103's
`status="hold"` attribute removed; the exact report remains the normal report.
The all-ready case changes that attribute to `status="ready"` and dispatches all
four identifiers. The first-held case changes ORD101 to `hold` and retains all
four. The empty fixture is `<queue/>` and reports `dispatch=; retained=`.
The position-cap fixture allows only position one: it reports
`dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104`.

entries.sampleCode:
Full synthetic catalog input. BOLT is deliberately placed before its referring
components to make document order visibly different from traversal order.

```xml
<catalog>
  <part id="KIT"><needs ref="FRAME"/><needs ref="MOTOR"/></part>
  <part id="BOLT"/>
  <part id="FRAME"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part>
  <part id="MOTOR"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part>
</catalog>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/product-dependency-closure/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $parts := parse-xml('<catalog><part id="KIT"><needs ref="FRAME"/><needs ref="MOTOR"/></part><part id="BOLT"/><part id="FRAME"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part><part id="MOTOR"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part></catalog>')/catalog/part
let $start := $parts[@id eq 'KIT']
let $step := function($part) { $parts[@id = $part/needs/@ref] }
let $reachable := transitive-closure($start, $step)
return concat('dependencies=', string-join($reachable/@id, ','), '; count=', count($reachable))
```

Exact output:

```text
dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/product-dependency-closure/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $parts := parse-xml('<catalog><part id="KIT"><needs ref="FRAME"/><needs ref="MOTOR"/></part><part id="BOLT"/><part id="FRAME"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part><part id="MOTOR"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part></catalog>')/catalog/part
return let $start := $parts[@id eq 'KIT']
return let $step := function($part) { $parts[@id = $part/needs/@ref] }
return let $reachable := fold-left(1 to count($parts), $step($start) | (), function($seen, $round) { $seen | ($seen ! $step(.)) })
return concat('dependencies=', string-join($reachable/@id, ','), '; count=', count($reachable))
```

Exact output:

```text
dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3
```

### Cycle input and result

Full input adds a link from BOLT back to KIT:

```xml
<catalog>
  <part id="KIT"><needs ref="FRAME"/><needs ref="MOTOR"/></part>
  <part id="BOLT"><needs ref="KIT"/></part>
  <part id="FRAME"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part>
  <part id="MOTOR"><needs ref="BOLT"/></part>
</catalog>
```

The [cycle expression](../examples/product-dependency-closure/cycle.xpath) reports:

```text
dependencies=KIT,BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=4
```

Each file embeds its full input and exact report or error marker.

| Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker |

| [main](../examples/product-dependency-closure/main.xpath) | `dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3` |

| [cycle](../examples/product-dependency-closure/cycle.xpath) | `dependencies=KIT,BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=4` |
| [self-cycle](../examples/product-dependency-closure/self-cycle.xpath) | `dependencies=KIT,BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=4` |
| [duplicate-edge](../examples/product-dependency-closure/duplicate-edge.xpath) | `dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3` |
| [leaf](../examples/product-dependency-closure/leaf.xpath) | `dependencies=; count=0` |
| [missing-start](../examples/product-dependency-closure/missing-start.xpath) | `dependencies=; count=0` |
| [include-start](../examples/product-dependency-closure/include-start.xpath) | `KIT,BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR` |
| [node-identity](../examples/product-dependency-closure/node-identity.xpath) | `true` |
| [non-node-start](../examples/product-dependency-closure/non-node-start.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [non-node-step](../examples/product-dependency-closure/non-node-step.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [multiple-starts](../examples/product-dependency-closure/multiple-starts.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [noncallable-step](../examples/product-dependency-closure/noncallable-step.xpath) | `XPTY0004` |
| [dangling-reference](../examples/product-dependency-closure/dangling-reference.xpath) | `dependencies=BOLT,MOTOR; count=2` |
| [reference-validation](../examples/product-dependency-closure/reference-validation.xpath) | `1` |

The dangling-reference fixture replaces FRAME's edge from KIT with MISSING.
Traversal reports only BOLT and MOTOR, because an unresolved edge selects no
node. The separate 3.1 validation expression counts one unresolved reference.
An empty closure from a missing start is likewise not proof of valid catalog data.
The node-identity check proves the returned BOLT is the original catalog node.

Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats.

**Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/product-map-index/main.xpath)

```xquery
(: A supplier snapshot contains a later correction for FILTER-A. :)
let $rows := (map{'sku':'FILTER-A','stock':12}, map{'sku':'SEAL-B','stock':0}, map{'sku':'FILTER-A','stock':8}),
    $index := map:build($rows, function($row){$row?sku}, function($row){$row?stock}, map{'duplicates':'use-last'}),
    $available := map:filter($index, function($sku,$stock,$position){$stock gt 0})
return string-join(map:entries($available) ! (let $entry := . return let $sku := map:keys($entry)[1] return concat($sku, '=', $entry($sku))), '|')
```

Expected text:

```text
FILTER-A=8
```

**Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/product-map-index/baseline.xpath)

```xquery
let $rows := (map{'sku':'FILTER-A','stock':12}, map{'sku':'SEAL-B','stock':0}, map{'sku':'FILTER-A','stock':8}),
    $index := map:merge($rows ! map:entry(?sku, ?stock), map{'duplicates':'use-last'})
return string-join(for $sku in sort(map:keys($index)) return if ($index($sku) gt 0) then concat($sku, '=', $index($sku)) else (), '|')
```

Expected text:

```text
FILTER-A=8
```

```

entries.sampleCode:
The synthetic carrier vocabulary below has one shipment header and ordered
event records. Each event supplies its shipment identity and state code. The
fixtures use document order as event order; production feeds must establish that
ordering before applying the checks. No timestamps, carrier standard, resource
access or application variables are assumed.

**Normal input:**

```xml
<history shipment="SHIP-42">
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/>
</history>
```

| Report field | Business check |
|---|---|
| `shipment`, `events` | Header identity and observed event count. |
| `consistent` | There is at least one event, every event has an identity, and all identities agree with the header. |
| `known` | Every event has a code and each code belongs to the declared vocabulary. |
| `start` | The first two events are CREATED then PICKED. |
| `dispatch` | PACKED immediately precedes DISPATCHED somewhere in the history. |
| `end` | DELIVERED is the final event. |
| `ready` | All five checks hold. This report flag is the demo's acceptance decision. |

**Complete XPath40 report — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/main.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true
```

**XPath31 comparison — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/baseline.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (count(distinct-values($ids)) le 1) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,1,2),('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := some $i in 1 to (count($codes)-1) satisfies deep-equal(subsequence($codes,$i,2),('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,count($codes),1),('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true
```

**Empty-history edge — mode 40:** [edge.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/edge.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=0;consistent=false;known=true;start=false;dispatch=false;end=false;ready=false
```

The edge input is `<history shipment="SHIP-42"/>`. Its `known=true` reflects
the vacuous universal check over no codes; `consistent=false` and the required
nonempty prefix/segment/suffix checks keep `ready=false`.

**Unexpected event input:**

```xml
<history shipment="SHIP-42">
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CUSTOMS"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/>
</history>
```

The complete [unexpected-event expression](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/unexpected-event.xpath)
uses the same report logic. CUSTOMS is outside this reduced vocabulary and breaks
the required adjacent dispatch pair. Its exact output is:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=false;start=true;dispatch=false;end=true;ready=false
```

entries.sampleCode:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>
```

### XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/supplier-offer-ranking/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $offers := parse-xml('<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>')/offers/offer
let $price := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@price) }
let $score := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@score) }
let $boundary := lowest($offers, (), $price)
let $cheapest := if (empty($boundary)) then () else $offers[$price(.) eq $price($boundary[1])]
let $collation := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return concat('cheapest=', string-join($cheapest/@id, ','), '; bestScore=', string-join(highest($offers, (), $score)/@id, ','), '; ranked=', string-join(sort-by($offers, (map {'key': $price}, map {'key': $score, 'order': 'descending'})) ! string(@id), ','), '; collationAvailable=', collation-available($collation))
```

Exact output:

```text
cheapest=B,C; bestScore=D; ranked=B,C,A,D; collationAvailable=true
```

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/supplier-offer-ranking/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $offers := parse-xml('<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>')/offers/offer
return let $cheap := min($offers/@price ! xs:decimal(.))
return let $best := max($offers/@score ! xs:decimal(.))
return let $byScore := sort($offers, (), function($o) { -xs:decimal($o/@score) })
return let $ranked := sort($byScore, (), function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@price) })
return concat('cheapest=', string-join($offers[xs:decimal(@price) eq $cheap]/@id, ','), '; bestScore=', string-join($offers[xs:decimal(@score) eq $best]/@id, ','), '; ranked=', string-join($ranked ! string(@id), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
cheapest=B,C; bestScore=D; ranked=B,C,A,D
```

let $received := unix-dateTime(xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds))
let $elapsed := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
let $budget := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds))
let $finished := $received + $elapsed
let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($elapsed), '; remainingSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($deadline - $finished), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)
```

Exact output:

```text
received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true
```

return let $received := xs:dateTime('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z') + xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0.001S') * xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds)
return let $elapsed := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * (xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
return let $budget := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds)
return let $finished := $received + $elapsed
return let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', ($elapsed div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; remainingSeconds=', (($deadline - $finished) div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)

Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<routes><archive server="files.example.test" folder="invoices" leaf="October 2026" value="//files.example.test/invoices/October%202026"/><partner host="api.example.test" value="https://demo:placeholder@api.example.test:443/legacy"/></routes>
```

Complete [main fixture](../examples/uri-option-policy/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $r := parse-xml('<routes><archive server="files.example.test" folder="invoices" leaf="October 2026" value="//files.example.test/invoices/October%202026"/><partner host="api.example.test" value="https://demo:placeholder@api.example.test:443/legacy"/></routes>')/routes
return let $archive := parse-uri(string($r/archive/@value), map {'unc-path': true()})
return let $api := parse-uri(string($r/partner/@value), map {'omit-default-ports': true()})
return let $target := build-uri(map {'scheme': $api?scheme, 'host': $api?host, 'port': $api?port, 'authority': 'ignored.example.test:8443', 'path': '/ignored', 'path-segments': ('', 'v2', 'invoices', 'INV/2048'), 'query': 'ignored=1', 'query-parameters': map {'status': 'ready now'}})
return concat('archive-scheme=', $archive?scheme, '; archive=', $archive?filepath, '; partner=', $target, '; userinfo=', exists($api?userinfo))
```

Output:

```text
archive-scheme=file; archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now; userinfo=false
```

The archive has no parsed host component under UNC policy. Partner password-bearing userinfo is absent and port 443 is omitted; the freshly built route overrides deliberately conflicting raw fields.

### XPath 3.1 comparison

Host-provided normalized archive metadata and validated HTTPS host allow this scoped construction:

```xpath
let $r := parse-xml('<routes><archive server="files.example.test" folder="invoices" leaf="October 2026" value="//files.example.test/invoices/October%202026"/><partner host="api.example.test" value="https://demo:placeholder@api.example.test:443/legacy"/></routes>')/routes
return let $archive := concat('//', $r/archive/@server, '/', $r/archive/@folder, '/', $r/archive/@leaf)
return let $target := concat('https://', $r/partner/@host, '/v2/invoices/', encode-for-uri('INV/2048'), '?status=', encode-for-uri('ready now'))
return concat('archive=', $archive, '; partner=', $target)
```

Output:

```text
archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now
```

This comparison constructs the two addresses; it does not produce parsed scheme/userinfo evidence. It requires the separate normalized attributes and an explicit host validation policy.

Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<picks><line id="A" aisle="B" bin="2" qty="2"/><line id="B" aisle="A" bin="10" qty="1"/><line id="C" aisle="A" bin="2" qty="3"/><line id="D" aisle="A" bin="2" qty="4"/></picks>
```

[XPath 4.0 runnable file](../examples/warehouse-pick-sorting/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<picks><line id="A" aisle="B" bin="2" qty="2"/><line id="B" aisle="A" bin="10" qty="1"/><line id="C" aisle="A" bin="2" qty="3"/><line id="D" aisle="A" bin="2" qty="4"/></picks>')/picks/line
return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return let $key := function($line) { (string($line/@aisle), xs:integer($line/@bin)) }
return let $ordered := sort($rows, $cp, $key)
return let $members := fold-left($rows, [], function($a, $line) { array:append($a, ($line, xs:integer($line/@qty))) })
return let $sorted := array:sort($members, $cp, function($member) { $key($member[1]) })
return concat('sequence=', string-join($ordered ! string(@id), ','), '; members=', string-join(for $i in 1 to array:size($sorted) return concat($sorted($i)[1]/@id, ':', $sorted($i)[2]), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
sequence=C,D,B,A; members=C:3,D:4,B:1,A:2
```

The [complete 3.1 runnable file](../examples/warehouse-pick-sorting/baseline.xpath)
contains the same expression and input; select `Compatibility31`. Its exact
output is also:

sequence=C,D,B,A; members=C:3,D:4,B:1,A:2
```

separate numeric-key probes, not in the intentionally portable report.

Additional executable catalog cases unpack invoice metadata and explicitly test
a missing currency key: [main](../examples/destructuring-let/main.xpath) produces
`INV-1042 / EUR`; [edge](../examples/destructuring-let/edge.xpath) returns missing
currency cardinality `0`. These run at `XPath40` and verify default-mode refusal.

Start with [the invoice chapter's practical migration pair](../worked-examples/invoice-to-erp/README.md#where-xpath-40-can-improve-readability): unpack invoice ID and currency from a metadata map to build a display label. Both complete expressions are supplied, engine-verified, and produce `INV-2026-1042 / EUR`. The 4.0 form requires explicit opt-in. The probes below cover the individual binding shapes.

~~~xquery
let $($x, $y) := (1, 2, 3) return ($x, $y)
  (: → (1, (2,3)) — last variable takes the rest :)

let $[$a, $b] := [3, 4, 5] return `a={$a} b={$b}`
  (: → "a=3 b=4" — surplus member 5 discarded :)

let $[$a, $b] := [1] return $b
  (: → FOAY0001 :)

let ${$name} := map {"name": "Braid"} return $name
  (: → "Braid" — key = variable local name :)

let $($x as xs:short, $y) := (42, "ok") return ($x, $y)
  (: → (42 xs:short, "ok") — PR 254 relabeling; annotation changes, datum untouched :)
~~~

The introductory input is declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/focus-functions/main.xpath) yields `12,5`. The [edge case](../examples/focus-functions/edge.xpath) yields `FORG0001 (expected error)`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context.


### Supplier delivery import and constructor audit

The [detailed example README](../examples/focus-functions/README.md) explains full input/output, field responsibilities, failures and compatibility. It links every published file and the [49-name audit inventory](../audit-focus-constructors.json). The new audit adds **508 executable checks** (including representative types, context/error/cardinality cases, 3.1 alternatives and experimental outcomes); the original three checks remain.

Input:

```xml
<deliveries><line id="A" quantity="12" price="2.50" date="2026-10-12" active="true"/><line id="B" quantity="5" price="4.00" date="2026-10-13" active="false"/></deliveries>
```

Complete [4.0 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-40.xpath):

```xquery
string-join(for $line in parse-xml('<deliveries><line id="A" quantity="12" price="2.50" date="2026-10-12" active="true"/><line id="B" quantity="5" price="4.00" date="2026-10-13" active="false"/></deliveries>')/deliveries/line return concat($line/@id, '|', $line/@quantity ! xs:integer(), '|', $line/@price ! xs:decimal(), '|', $line/@date ! xs:date(), '|', $line/@active ! xs:boolean()), ';')
```

Output (id, quantity, price, promised date, active flag):

```text
A|12|2.5|2026-10-12|true;B|5|4|2026-10-13|false
```

The [3.1 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-31.xpath) uses explicit `(.)` constructor arguments and produces identical output. Both empty-input reports return an empty string; reordered input retains document order. Quantity `twelve` refuses FORG0001 in both versions. These reports normalize values; they do not apply required-field, schema or business-total validation.

Empty simple-map input means no call occurs. It differs from a missing context item (XPDY0002 for every zero-arity constructor), explicit empty argument (empty result for every one-argument constructor), and a multi-item argument (tested integer refusal XPTY0004). Mapping two lexical inputs invokes the constructor once per item: scalar types produce two values; ENTITIES/IDREFS/NMTOKENS produce four for two two-token inputs.

All 48 inhabited types pass representative value/type checks. `xs:error` is registered but has no non-empty value space; its non-empty calls refuse FORG0001 and its explicit empty argument returns empty. This is not a missing constructor implementation. String-like types have no generic invalid lexical string; their invalid-input checks use a map and report FOTY0013. Additional numeric bounds, timezone, QName binding, array atomization and wrong-source-type cases are documented in the README. Testing one lexical sample per type does not establish exhaustive XML Schema casting conformance.

**Pinned contract review:** [F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/xpath-functions.xml), sections `constructor-functions-for-xsd-types`, `constructor-functions-for-xsd-list-types`, `constructor-functions-for-xsd-union-types`, plus QName rules. Default argument is the context item; list/union contracts remain distinct. This current comparison does not recover the historically adopted pin. Source: [generated registrations and XsFocusCtor](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); coercion: [VM engine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs).

Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4.
entries.sampleCode: The complete [4.0 report](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) reads [normal.xml](../examples/numeric-literals/normal.xml): readings A(flags5,count1500), B(flags2,count900). It emits `A:ready|B:hold|ready=1;total=2400`, matching the3.0 baseline. Empty input emits `ready=0;total=0`; reordering changes row order; invalid count `oops` raises FORG0001.
